fields.aka: Jāhnavā Devī, Jāhnavā Mātā, Jāhnavī, Īśvarī
fields.disciples: Vīrabhadra Gosvāmī, Rāmāi Gosāi, Śrīmatī Devī
fields.notes:
Younger wife (śakti) of Śrī Nityānanda, with her elder sister Vasudhā; daughter of Sūryadāsa Sarakhela of Śāligrāma; niece of Gaurīdāsa Paṇḍita. No children of her own; brought up Kānu Ṭhākura and adopted Rāmāi Gosāi; guru of her stepson Vīrabhadra. After the Lord's associates she led the Vaiṣṇavas: presided over the Kheturī festival, went twice to Vṛndāvana (Bhakti-ratnākara 10-13), found Śrī Gopīnātha in the Ganges (now at Jirāṭ).

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Revatī; also Anaṅga-mañjarī (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 65-66).

Other Jāhnavās (wife of Puruṣottama dāsa; mother of Kāśīnātha of Cātarā) have their own records.

Elder wife of Śrī Nityānanda and elder daughter of Sūryadāsa Sarakhela; sister of Jāhnavā Devī. Mother of Vīracandra (Vīrabhadra Gosvāmī) and Gaṅgā Devī. Named in the Vaiṣṇava-vandanās of Jīva (41-42), Devakīnandana (12) and Vṛndāvana dāsa (15).

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Vāruṇī, Balarāma's consort; some say Anaṅga-mañjarī (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 65-66).

fields.appearance: Agrahāyaṇa Śukla Caturdaśī (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna; the texts: Kārtika Kṛṣṇa Navamī), at Khaḍadaha
fields.notes:
Son of Śrī Nityānanda and Vasudhā; sister Gaṅgā Devī; disciple of Jāhnavā Mātā. «After Nityānanda the greatest branch» (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 11.8-12). Married Śrīmatī and Nārāyaṇī, daughters of Yadunandana Ācārya of Jhāmaṭapura (Bhakti-ratnākara 13). Sons and disciples: Gopījana-vallabha (Latā), Rāmakṛṣṇa (Gaṇeśapura, Māldaha), Rāmacandra (Khaḍadaha); daughter Bhuvanamohinī. Went to Vṛndāvana; organised the Vaiṣṇavas of Bengal; excommunicated Jayagopāla dāsa; forbade the cūḍā (the Cūḍādhārīs).

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Kṣīrodakaśāyī (Payodhiśāyī) Viṣṇu, an expansion of Saṅkarṣaṇa; also Niśaṭha and Ulmuka (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 67).

Daughter of Śrī Nityānanda and Vasudhā; sister of Vīrabhadra. Wife of Mādhava Ācārya (Mādhava Caṭṭopādhyāya) of Jirāṭ; son Gopīvallabha, from whom the Gosvāmīs of the Gaṅgā-vaṁśa of Jirāṭ descend. Abhirāma Ṭhākura wrote his Gaṅgā-stotra about her.

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: the river Gaṅgā; her husband was King Śantanu (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 69).

Not Gaṅgā Devī, mother of Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi (her own record).

Husband of Gaṅgā Devī, daughter of Śrī Nityānanda (Prema-vilāsa 19; Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 11.52). Father Viśveśvara Caṭṭopādhyāya, mother Mahālakṣmī, who died at his birth; brought up by Bhagīratha Ācārya and Jayadurgā Devī of Nanda-grāma near Katwa, while his father took sannyāsa (Prema-vilāsa 21). Son: Gopīvallabha.

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: King Śantanu (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 69).

The Mādhava Ācāryas of Caitanya's and of Gadādhara's branches have their own records.

fields.name: Sūryadāsa Sarakhela
fields.aka: Sūryadāsa Paṇḍita, Suryadasa Paṇḍit, Sarakhela Sūryadāsa
fields.notes:
Of Nityānanda's branch (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 11.25). Son of Kaṁsāri Miśra and Kamalā Devī; brothers Dāmodara, Jagannātha, Gaurīdāsa Paṇḍita, Kṛṣṇadāsa and Nṛsiṁha-Caitanya. Wife: Bhadrāvatī. Accountant of the king of Gauḍa, hence the title Sarakhela. Gave his daughters Vasudhā and Jāhnavā to Śrī Nityānanda after a dream (Bhakti-ratnākara 12).

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: King Kakudmī (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 65).

fields.name: Hāḍāi Paṇḍita
fields.aka: Hāḍāi Ojhā, Hāḍāi Ṭhākura, Mukunda Ojhā, Hadai Ṭhākura, Hadai Ṭhākura (Mukunda Ojha Haddipa Paṇḍita)
fields.notes:
Father of Śrī Nityānanda; wife Padmāvatī Devī; seven sons, Nityānanda the eldest (Prema-vilāsa 24). A brāhmaṇa of the line of Nārāyaṇa Bhaṭṭa Caturvedī (Śāṇḍilya gotra); son of Sundaramalla Bāḍurī (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna). Gave his twelve-year-old son to a sannyāsī who begged for Him.

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Vasudeva, Balarāma's father; in Rāma-līlā Daśaratha (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 40).

Mother of Śrī Nityānanda; wife of Hāḍāi Paṇḍita; daughter of King Mukuṭa Rāya of Mauḍeśvara. Gave her twelve-year-old son to a sannyāsī at her husband's word (Caitanya-bhāgavata Madhya 3.93).

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Rohiṇī, Balarāma's mother; in Rāma-līlā Sumitrā (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 40).

Not Padmāvatī (Gaurāṅgapriyā), wife of Śrīnivāsa Ācārya.

Adopted son and disciple of Jāhnavā Mātā; son of Caitanya dāsa and grandson of Vaṁśīvadana Ṭhākura, «the second Vaṁśīvadana». Brought the Deities of Kānāi-Balāi from Vraja and installed them at Bāghnāpāḍā; a lifelong brahmacārī; initiated his younger brother Śacīnandana and gave him the Deities' service.

fields.aka: Kānu Ṭhākura, Kānāi Ṭhākura, Śiśu Kṛṣṇadāsa, Kānudāsa
fields.appearance: Āṣāḍha Śukla Dvitīyā (Ratha-yātrā), 1531 CE (other texts: 1450 or 1457 Śaka)
fields.notes: Son of Puruṣottama dāsa Ṭhākura and Jāhnavā, grandson of Sadāśiva Kavirāja (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 11.39-40). His mother died after his birth; Nityānanda named him Śiśu Kṛṣṇadāsa and Jāhnavā Mātā brought him up at Khaḍadaha and took him to Vṛndāvana, where Jīva Gosvāmī called him Kānāi Ṭhākura. His anklet fell at Bodhkhānā. Descendants at Bodhkhānā and Bhājanghāṭ; disciple Śrīrāma. Songs signed Kānudāsa / Kānurāma dāsa (Padakalpataru).
